name: Floor Dumbbell Flye to Press
description: A combination chest exercise performed on the floor that begins as a dumbbell flye and transitions into a press on each repetition. The floor limits elbow travel below shoulder level, reducing shoulder stress while still providing significant chest stretch. The flye-to-press combo increases time under tension and trains both adduction and horizontal pushing in a single movement.

execution.starting_position: Lie on the floor with knees bent, feet flat. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above the chest with palms facing each other.
execution.setup_instructions: Select a weight appropriate for a flye — lighter than pressing weight. The floor prevents excessive arm travel below the torso.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended above the chest, dumbbells nearly touching, palms facing each other.
Step 2: Open the arms out wide in a flye arc, lowering until the upper arms contact or near the floor.
Step 3: At the bottom of the flye, bend the elbows and bring the dumbbells to chest level (now in press position).
Step 4: Press the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Step 5: That is one rep: flye open → elbows bend → press up. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the flye open, exhale on the press back up.
common_mistakes: Opening too fast and slamming arms into the floor
Using too heavy a weight for the flye portion — leads to poor form on the arc
Skipping the elbow bend at the bottom — this is what distinguishes the combo from a pure flye
safety_considerations: The floor stops elbow travel and protects the shoulder naturally — do not force past the floor stop
Keep elbows slightly bent throughout the flye arc
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open to floor contact on the flye. Press to full arm extension. Floor contact provides natural range of motion limit.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-1-1 (2s flye open, 1s bend elbows, 1s press, 1s reset)
coaching_cues: Flye first, then press — the two phases are distinct within each rep
Soft elbows on the flye — do not lock the arms straight
